newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - Feb 21.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - Feb 21.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Building industry unions and employers in Victoria are poised to gain what is known as "portable" sick leave entitlements for construction workers. Under the scheme, building workers would be allowed to transfer accrued sick leave entitlements from employer to employer. Page 3.

The Nine Network, traditional stalwarts of Australian cricket broadcasts, will challenge the Australian Broadcasting Authority in the Federal Court today over anti-siphoning provisions in the television rights to Australia's cricket tour of South Africa. Pay-TV operator, Foxtel, and the Seven network have reached a broadcast agreement of the Australian tour. Page 2.

A Queensland regional university is aiming to bypass unions to register what is believed to be the first non-union enterprise agreement brokered under the Federal Government's controversial industrial relations laws. Page 3. --

Company profits increased to a record high in the December quarter with further figures released yesterday hinted at a speeding up of the Labour market. Net profit for the period increased 8.6 per cent to A$12 billion while a skilled vacancy survey prepard by the Federal employment department showed a fourth consecutive monthly increase, rising 0.7 per cent. Page 5.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Australian Prime Minister, John Howard, yesterday paid tribute to Deng Xiaoping after the world learned of the death of one China's last great revolutionary. Howard said Deng's legacy was China's growing prosperity. The Chinese leadership projected an image of stability when Australian officials, in Beijing to prepare for the visit of Howard at Easter, were informed the trip will still proceed to plan. Page 1.

An increase in company profits to the highest level in over a decade have increased Federal Government hopes that economic activity is on the pick-up. Figures released by the Australian Bureau of Statistics reveal an 8.6 per cent gain in profits for the Dcember quarter 1996. This figure far outstripped economists predictions of between a 3 per cent fall and a 2.5 per cent rise in seasonally adjusted profits before tax, depreciation and interest. Page 2.

A member of the nation's peak medical research body, the National Health and Medical Research Council, Dr Peter McCullagh yesterday backed Federal Cabinet's recent veto of Professor John Funder as chairman to the council. McCullagh, a member of the ethicscommittee, said Funder's performance as an adviser to a previous high level research school "left more than something to be desired". Page 3.

Backbench and Senate pressure has forced an embarrassing backdown for the Federal Government in its reforms to education benefit, Austudy. An extra 8500 students and families will be eligible for increased benefits after the Education, Employment and Traiing Department loosens assessment on means testing and streamlines its administration procedures. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Education Minister Amanda Vanstone conceded yesterday that changes to the student allowance, Austudy, means test were too harsh as she apologised to more than 100,000 students whose requests for financial assistance were to be rejected. The embarrassing bckdown followed a rare backbench revolt from Coalition members who claimed reforms to means testing went too far. Page 3.

It was the answer to the one question that every visitor of the Sydney Aquarium asks when a glass tank cracked yesterday. The Darling Harbour water-world gushed out 12,000 litres of seawater and six sharks as several tourists were hit by a "wall of water. Aquarium staff acted quickly to drag the sharks and other marine life to other tanks while six people were treated for minor injuries. Page3.

A group of Sydney mayors has called on the NSW Government to step in and negotiate an alternative to the controversial A$200 million apartment development proposed for East Circular Quay on Australia's most recognised harbourfront. Page 3.

Eleven months into its first term, and despite a number of political slip-ups, the Federal Government is further in front of the Labor party in opinion polls than it was in the landslide March 1996 election. On a national two-party split the Coalition leds Labor 54-46, 2 points more than the March 1996 result. Page 2.
THE AGE

A new wave of Chinese leaders today faces the challenge of steering the one of the world's most powerful nations following the death of paramount leader Deng Xiaoping. Following a week of rumours that suggested Deng was critically ill, the China News Ageny announced early yesterday that the 92-year-old Long March veteran had died at 9.08pm on Wednesday. Australian political leaders - including Prime Minister John Howard - paid tribute to the communist leader. Page 1

Victorian Premier, Jeff Kennett has refused to censure his police minister, Bill McGrath, over his controversial comments that he had great reservations about gays and lesbians in the police force. Kennett refused to accept the avalanche of criticism from community groups, claiming that "everyone's entitled to an opinion". Page 1.

The ongoing row over television rights to Australia's cricket tour of South Africa was resolved last night in a deal which will see the entire three-Test series broadcast on Network Seven. The deal is being hailed as a victory by the Federal Government who has been trying to keep big Australian sports events on free-to-air television. Page 1.

A parliamentary committee was told that the Federal Government would be failing its international human rights obligations as well as its most vulnerable citizens if it did not solve the continuing stand-off with the states over legal aid funding. Federal sex discrimination commissioner, Sue Walpole, told the Senate committee that minority groups would suffer as a direct result of the cuts. Page A2.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
